explanation: The recorded failure was a route-budget mismatch, not an observed obstacle: every self-occluded review reduced progress to 0.035 m, so five reviews exhausted the route loop while the robot remained safely above the carton. This repair preserves the executed approach and historical measured invariants. It obtains one explicit authorization for each bounded local phase, separates self-occlusion from external obstruction, and executes that phase in at most six 0.08 m pose-feedback segments. It does not require visibility of the later transfer corridor or direct visibility of both vertical contact faces before an open-jaw staging descent. Measured grasp width, conservative aperture estimate, table clearance, and pad overlap are supplied explicitly to the reviewer. Intermediate noncontact registrations provide new object observations and tracker appearance updates during descent; unexpected carton displacement stops the approach. Existing retention testing, release verification, bounded observation recovery, checkpoints, and Jev direction questions remain intact.
interface: Patch to the existing executable main(api); no scene reset or motion is performed by submission. At execution, the existing initialization recalls placement_episode, obtains fresh carton geometry and tracker initialization, and revalidates stationary bowl references. Returns JSON-compatible completion_proposed and evidence. Uses the existing exact structured review schemas and documented API operations. route now obtains authorization for a specified local phase, executes up to six feedback segments of at most 0.08 m, and reports numerical remaining distance if that finite bound is exhausted. One explicitly authorized 0.025 m upward observation move and reassessment remain available per route. Entirely unobserved immediate motion, observed obstruction, insufficient evidence, control failure, or inconsistent object motion stops the method. Grasp diagnostics and reference measurements remain checkpointed historical assertions, not current sensor truth. Noncontact approach segments refresh the RGB-D tracker and check the stationary-object dependency; carrying segments continue to compare object motion against actual hand motion. Post-release observations and physical settling still determine the completion proposal.
jev_protocol: The seven existing physical-control questions are unchanged: x, y, z, rx, ry, rz select negative, hold, or positive from their explicitly bound world-axis goal_relation; gripper selects exactly open, close, or keep from objective.gripper. Jev receives measured robot state, numerical pose residuals, and program phase, pad-center semantics, uncertainty, and historical retention evidence. Python computes targets, transforms, bounds, and tolerances; the host dispatches Jev's unchanged choices using documented bounded residual magnitudes. Ordinary local segments use drive; contact updates use bounded control loops. reached establishes pose and command delivery only, moved may continue within the finite loop, and stalled or lease exhaustion stops without repeatedly pushing. Structured image reviews authorize only the named local phase: external=present identifies an observed external obstruction, none_seen means no obstruction observed rather than certified clearance, and unknown means no usable assessment. visibility explicitly distinguishes observed, partial_unobserved, self_occluded, and unobserved space. advance requires an evidence-supported local phase and does not become invalid solely because the robot hides part of the view. view_up authorizes only one specified upward observation move, followed by reassessment; stop prohibits route motion. Code supplies grasp geometry and clearance estimates instead of asking Jev to calculate them. Registration, hand displacement, object displacement, and attachment error remain separate from grasp and final placement claims.
